landscape.hook: Can you explain #expect, Confirmation and Expected Count in English?

dialogue.title: Did the callback fire twice?
dialogue.setting: Moving tests from XCTest to Swift Testing

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, I move our tests from XCTest to Swift Testing. What replaces the asserts?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Use #expect. It checks a condition and records a failure if it is false.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Nice. And the old expectation for my callback?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Use a confirmation. It counts how often an event happens while the async test runs.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: In my code, I call `ok` inside the closure?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. Each call to `ok` is one event.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: My callback should fire twice. Can the test check that?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Set the expected count to two. The test fails if the count is different.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: What if it fires three times?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then the confirmation fails, too. The expected count is exact.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Good. #expect for values, a confirmation for events.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And an expected count for how many times.
